gold_text.613.7b: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is usually done using a timestamp system. An effect with an earlier timestamp is applied before an effect with a later timestamp. A continuous effect generated by the resolution of a spell or ability receives a timestamp at the time it’s created.
gold_text.613.7f: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is usually done using a timestamp system. An effect with an earlier timestamp is applied before an effect with a later timestamp. A permanent receives a new timestamp each time it turns face up or face down.

answer_gold: It's a 4/4 black Frog with trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature", but no other abilities. Wayward Angel receives a new timestamp when it turns face up, so its ability is applied before Turn to Frog in each layer. Wayward Angel's last ability is removed by Turn to Frog in layer 6, but since it's already started to apply in layer 5 to change its color to black, it will continue doing so in later layers. Turn to Frog has the earlier timestamp, so it makes Wayward Angel blue before it becomes black in layer 5 and removes Wayward Angel's abilities in layer 6 before it gains trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature".

question: Ahmad controls [Conspiracy] (naming "Ferret"), [Kormus Bell], [Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth], and a [Vastwood Zendikon] enchanting Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth that entered the battlefield in that order. Is Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth a creature? If so, what are its creature types?
answer:
Direct answer, unchanged: Yes — Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is a creature, and its only creature type is Ferret (a 6/4 green Ferret creature Swamp land under Ahmad's control).

Important honesty note about grounding: the numbered Comprehensive Rules excerpts I was given deal almost entirely with control, ownership, and player-controlling effects (for example [613.1b], which only lists Layer 2, control-changing effects). None of the provided numbered rules cover type-changing effects, Layer 4, or timestamp/dependency ordering. So this answer does not rest on the numbered rules; it rests entirely on the card texts and the card rulings provided, which are authoritative on their own:

- Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: "Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types" — this includes Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth itself while on the battlefield ([Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth ruling #0], [Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth ruling #2]).
- Kormus Bell: "All Swamps are 1/1 black creatures that are still lands," affecting every player's Swamps ([Kormus Bell ruling #1]), so Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is simultaneously a land and a creature ([Kormus Bell ruling #0]).
- Vastwood Zendikon: "Enchanted land is a 6/4 green Elemental creature. It's still a land." Its later power/toughness-setting overwrites Kormus Bell's 1/1 ([Vastwood Zendikon ruling #0]); the permanent is both land and creature ([Vastwood Zendikon ruling #5]).
- Conspiracy (Ferret chosen): "Creatures you control are the chosen type," and affected creatures lose all their other creature types ([Conspiracy ruling #4]); it can grant a creature type to animated lands ([Conspiracy ruling #1]). Conspiracy can only apply once something is a creature, so it applies after Kormus Bell and Vastwood Zendikon have made Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth a creature — stripping Elemental and leaving Ferret as its only creature type.

Conspiracy changes only creature types, so the land type Swamp granted by Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth remains. Being a Ferret grants no abilities ([Conspiracy ruling #3]), and Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth can attack or use {T} abilities only if Ahmad has controlled it continuously since the beginning of his most recent turn ([Kormus Bell ruling #2]).

The answer is identical in two-player and multiplayer games: Kormus Bell affects all players' Swamps and Conspiracy affects only creatures Ahmad controls; [613.1b] (control-changing effects in Layer 2) is the only provided layer rule and no control change is happening here.

gold_text.205.1b: The type line is printed directly below the illustration. It contains the card’s card type(s). It also contains the card’s subtype(s) and supertype(s), if applicable. Some effects change an object’s card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, supertype, or subtype. In such cases, all the object’s prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained. This rule applies to effects that use phrases such as “in addition to its other types” or that state that something is “still a [type, supertype, or subtype].” Some effects state that an object becomes an “artifact creature”; these effects also allow the object to retain all of its prior card types and subtypes. Some effects state that an object becomes a “[creature type or types] artifact creature”; these effects also allow the object to retain all of its prior card types and subtypes other than creature types, but replace any existing creature types. An ability reads, “All lands are 1/1 creatures that are still lands.” The affected lands now have two card types: creature and land. If there were any lands that were also artifacts before the ability’s effect applied to them, those lands would become “artifact land creatures,” not just “creatures,” or “land creatures.” The effect allows them to retain both the artifact and land card types. In addition, each land affected by the ability retains any land types and supertypes it had before the ability took effect. An ability reads, “All artifacts are 1/1 artifact creatures.” If a permanent is both an artifact and an enchantment, it will become an artifact enchantment creature.
gold_text.613.7d: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is usually done using a timestamp system. An effect with an earlier timestamp is applied before an effect with a later timestamp. An object receives a timestamp at the time it enters a zone.
gold_text.613.8a: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is sometimes done using a dependency system. If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system. An effect is said to “depend on” another if (a) it’s applied in the same layer (and, if applicable, sublayer) as the other effect; (b) applying the other would change the text or the existence of the first effect, what it applies to, or what it does to any of the things it applies to; and (c) neither effect is from a characteristic-defining ability or both effects are from characteristic-defining abilities. Otherwise, the effect is considered to be independent of the other effect.
gold_text.613.8b: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is sometimes done using a dependency system. If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system. An effect dependent on one or more other effects waits to apply until just after all of those effects have been applied. If multiple dependent effects would apply simultaneously in this way, they’re applied in timestamp order relative to each other. If several dependent effects form a dependency loop, then this rule is ignored and the effects in the dependency loop are applied in timestamp order.
gold_text.613.8c: Within a layer or sublayer, determining which order effects are applied in is sometimes done using a dependency system. If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system. After each effect is applied, the order of remaining effects is reevaluated and may change if an effect that has not yet been applied becomes dependent on or independent of one or more other effects that have not yet been applied.

answer_gold: It is an Elemental Ferret creature. Conspiracy has the earliest timestamp, but it's dependent on Vastwood Zendikon, and waits to apply until after Vastwood Zendikon is applied. Kormus Bell is dependent on Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth, so Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is applied first, then Kormus Bell. At this point Conspiracy is no longer be dependent on Vastwood Zendikon, so Conspiracy is applied, and then Vastwood Zendikon. Since Vastwood Zendikon says that Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is still a land, it retains its prior creature type of "Ferret" when it becomes an Elemental.
